direction.label: Precision Instrument — authority correction
direction.hypothesis: Externalizing the amber approval gate while preserving the relay silhouette makes the strongest direction truthful enough for human identity review

asset.surface: Starlight Research Team character direction review

prompt.primary_request: Correct the Precision Instrument candidate's authority signaling without replacing its successful Lyra identity or relay morphology
prompt.scene: The same restrained black calibration chamber with one physical human approval control mounted on the wall beyond Lyra
prompt.subject: Lyra as the same full-body porcelain-and-obsidian research relay holding the same tangible multi-input routing instrument
prompt.style_medium: high-fidelity cinematic industrial character design render with editorial restraint
prompt.composition: preserve the full-body eye-level portrait and clear silhouette, with the router visible at working height and no pedestal
prompt.lighting_mood: precise soft key light, calm competence, crisp material separation, restrained machine activity
prompt.color_palette: aged ivory porcelain, obsidian black, restrained ink blue, narrow cyan channels, one external warm amber control
prompt.materials_textures: matte porcelain grain, exposed black mechanisms, brushed titanium, precise seams, minimal functional textile
constraints: preserve the faceplate cranium body proportions and full-body composition
preserve the multi-input router and blue activity channels
make the chest center completely unlit matte obsidian with no warm glow
show amber only on one physical wall-mounted human approval control separate from the robot
simplify the radial collar into functional relay vanes rather than ceremonial decoration
avoid: amber light anywhere on or inside the robot
glowing chest core or heart trope
human pictogram or fake interface panel
crown halo ruff or royal collar
superhero stance or generic sci-fi armor
prompt.final_prompt: Use case: identity-preserve edit. Asset type: 4:5 Starlight character direction refinement. Image 1 is the owned Lyra Precision Instrument v1 edit target. Preserve the same Lyra faceplate, segmented ivory cranium, full-body eye-level composition, porcelain-and-obsidian anatomy, calm stance, narrow cyan arm channels, articulated hands, and physical multi-input router. Make only these corrections: remove every amber or warm light from Lyra's body; replace the glowing chest center with a completely unlit matte-obsidian relay socket; simplify the shoulder collar into thinner functional routing vanes rather than a ceremonial ruff; replace the wall human pictogram with one clearly physical wall-mounted amber approval lever or witness lamp, separate from and behind the robot. Cyan remains machine activity. Amber appears only on the external human-owned control. Keep the restrained black calibration chamber, crisp material separation, generous edge safety, no pedestal. Matte porcelain grain, exposed black mechanics, brushed titanium, precise seams. No text, no logos, no fake UI, no human icon, no glowing chest, no halo, no crown, no royal symbolism, no weapons, no combat armor, no superhero stance, no global glow.

qa.strongest_element: The role stays immediately legible while cyan machine activity and the physical external amber approval control now express the authority boundary truthfully
qa.weakest_element: The exposed collar rods feel appended rather than engineered into the anatomy, and the generated portrait is taller than the requested four-to-five master crop
qa.next_change: Use this as the governance-correct base, integrate lower-profile relay vanes into the shoulder anatomy, and regenerate or art-direct a true four-to-five master
